failed_step: Execute both SDK consumers against the hash-bound AAR on the selected ART runtime
observed: Full SDK instrumentation reported three passed cases and its cleanup subsequently confirmed absence.
Minimal runtimeVersionOnly instrumentation reported pass. Its later installed-APK verification retained zero-exit reads of 26112 and 11776 bytes instead of 13702871.
The first missing transport was re-registered once. It failed again and cleanup never established removal, so the job correctly failed and retired its failed runtime receipt.
Before the first outage and after its first recovery, boot ID, adbd PID 430 and system_server PID 547 match. The second outage has no successful final guest-state capture.
not_proven: A root cause for either ADB transport loss; the transport read/write-failure logs do not identify it.
An SDK native crash, adbd kill, guest reboot or causal LMKD explanation. Prior no-SDK controls also had LMKD kills and succeeded.
Completion of the Android 16KiB runtime/cleanup gate or the dependent replay. Instrumentation pass is not overall qualification.

follow_up.change: Compare direct-file capture with the unchanged production bounded_process.write_stdout_at engine in the existing no-SDK file-copy control. Preserve 12 samples per method, guest hash brackets, deadlines and failure reporting; alternate which method runs first.
follow_up.basis: Previous successful no-SDK file copies used subprocess stdout directly to a file. The failing installed-APK reader uses the bounded pipe writer. This controlled comparison narrows a real harness difference without changing the production admission or cleanup rules.

retention_scope: Complete failure-diagnostic ZIP and selected job/analysis/control-test metadata are in this capture. The verified complete 47-MB runtime artifact and job console remain under target; no APK, native-library binary or device secret is republished in this checkpoint.

same_source_ci_observation.scope: Successful job status at the same source head; the PR merge has an identical Git tree. This is not a controlled same-binary comparison and does not diagnose either transport failure. The original PR failure remains failure.
